briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East saw a sharp escalation in Israeli-Lebanese hostilities, with Israel conducting extensive airstrikes in southern Lebanon, reportedly killing at least 11 and wounding 20, in response to a Hezbollah drone attack. Concurrently, Iran significantly heightened its rhetoric and actions regarding the Strait of Hormuz, claiming a missile test over a US carrier and declaring an impending "restricted zone," while the US announced it had redirected 92 commercial vessels and disabled three Iranian oil tankers. These developments underscore a region on the brink, with multiple flashpoints nearing critical thresholds.

IRAN
Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, claimed that 48 hours prior, an Iranian anti-destroyer missile was tested "right above a US carrier," forcing US forces to flee. Rezaei also announced that Iran would declare a new "restricted zone" in the Persian Gulf in the coming days, extending beyond the area of the US naval blockade, and warned that any vessel entering without coordination would face Iranian sanctions. He further asserted Iran's right to respond to a "bloody American crime" at a wedding in Sirikh last week and claimed US economic warfare impacts sovereignty and free trade, while denying a major famine due to the US blockade. Separately, Iran's Parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Commission approved a plan to ban countries imposing sanctions from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Major General Ali Abdollahi, Commander of the Iranian Armed Forces, vowed Iran would "never cave to US pressure," calling American expectations "a false illusion."

Economically, the Iranian government officially increased fuel prices for "heavy consumers" (over 110 liters/month) by 100% from 50,000 to 100,000 Rials per liter, effective Tuesday, 10 September. The government also announced that the "third tier" gasoline price (for non-personal fuel cards) would increase to 10,000 Tomans (100,000 Rials), effective 00:00, 17 Shahrivar (07 September 2026). These announcements led to kilometer-long queues at petrol stations across the country. The official dollar exchange rate in the free market reached over 227,000 Tomans, briefly touching 230,000 Tomans before retracting. Trump claimed Iran's oil exports had fallen to zero, though data from Kepler indicated average daily traffic through Hormuz had decreased significantly to 10 vessels, with only 2 on Saturday and 6 on Sunday, largely through Iranian-controlled waters. Two servicemen, Abolfazl Oudi and Keyvan Ramroudi, from the Martyr Mirhossaini Operational Headquarters, were martyred in an attack in the Kourin area of Zahedan, Sistan and Baluchestan province. The IRGC Intelligence Organization identified and arrested an eight-member sabotage network in Fars province, confiscating firearms and ammunition.

ISRAEL
The IDF conducted a snap drill, 'Breaking Dawn 2.0,' designed to test the General Staff's decision-making in a multi-front, complex scenario. This included a simulated infiltration of 10-15 terrorists from Lebanon, a terror attack on Route 60 in the West Bank, a West Bank settlement infiltration, rocket attacks on Tel Aviv, and fighting along the Yellow Line in Gaza, culminating in a simulated breach of Israeli territory from Gaza into three border communities. Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir stated the drill was a "message to our enemies" and that the IDF is "capable, prepared and ready to defend the State of Israel." An initial debriefing found "very good" overall readiness.

Overnight, the IDF struck Hamas sites in Gaza in response to an explosive device that hit an engineering vehicle on the Israeli side of the "Yellow Line" in northern Gaza, causing no injuries. The IDF termed this a "blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement." In the West Bank, a joint IDF, Yamam, and Shin Bet operation in Aqqaba village targeted a Hamas cell, apprehending 10 operatives and locating a rocket (without a launcher) and significant quantities of M-16 weapons and explosives, which were destroyed. In other West Bank incidents, Omar Tubasi, 20, was killed by settler fire in Hajjah village, and two suspects were arrested in connection with an attack in Qusra, one a 19-year-old from the Shomron area and the other an 18-year-old IDF soldier from the Jordan Valley.

Domestically, a large-scale security exercise began in the Eilat and Arava region to practice extreme scenarios, including surprise attacks and multiple fronts, as part of lessons learned from October 7. The Israeli National Security Council warned of ongoing terrorist threats against Israeli citizens and Jewish communities abroad ahead of the upcoming Jewish holidays. Political developments included the Likud tribunal ruling that Ati Atiya would be 20th and Gila Gamliel 25th on the party list. Gadi Eisenkot's "Yeshar!" party announced its Knesset list, including former security officials and families of hostages and fallen soldiers. Ayelet Shaked decided not to run in the upcoming elections. Defense Minister Ben Gvir stated he would not approve senior police appointments before elections, which the Deputy AG questioned for political involvement; however, the Police Chief completed the first round of appointments regardless. The Central Elections Committee overturned a ban on real-time reporting from polling stations. Fuel prices in Israel are set to decrease by 50 agorot to 7.75 NIS/liter from midnight.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, Israeli airstrikes targeted Hamas infrastructure and locations in central Gaza, northern Gaza, Shati refugee camp, and Khan Yunis, reportedly killing Hamas commander Yousef Akilah ("Abu al-Walid"), identified as a former personal bodyguard of Yahya Sinwar. These strikes were in response to a Hamas-placed IED that hit an IDF engineering vehicle in the "Yellow Line" area in northern Gaza, which the IDF deemed a "blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement." Palestinian sources reported casualties in these strikes. A mass funeral was held in Zeitoun neighborhood for 100 martyrs whose bodies were recovered from under rubble. The Palestinian Center for Missing and Forcibly Disappeared Persons condemned Israel's unauthorized clearance of debris as a "moral execution" of thousands still missing.

In the West Bank, a joint IDF, Yamam, and Shin Bet operation in Aqqaba village led to the apprehension of 10 Hamas operatives and the discovery of a rocket without a launcher, an M-16 assault rifle, and significant explosive materials. These weapons were destroyed on site by police sappers. In Hajjah village, Omar Tubasi, 20, was reportedly killed by settler fire. Police and Shin Bet arrested two additional suspects, a 19-year-old from the Shomron area and an 18-year-old IDF soldier from the Jordan Valley, in connection with an assault in Qusra village.

LEBANON
Southern Lebanon experienced a significant escalation of Israeli airstrikes. Lebanese media reported 11 dead and 5 wounded in overnight Israeli airstrikes in Kfar Reman, including 9 killed (2 children) in a residential building strike and 2 Amal movement paramedics killed in a drone strike on a car. Other strikes hit Nabatieh and Arab Salim, and a building in Deir al-Zahrani was destroyed after an evacuation warning. Lebanese health authorities later updated the casualty count to 4 dead and 20 wounded from Israeli strikes since morning. The IDF confirmed striking Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon in response to a Hezbollah drone attack on troops in the Ali Taher Ridge area, which caused no Israeli casualties. Targets included weapon depots, buildings used for planning terror activities, and a command center in a former hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, from which Hezbollah operatives involved in "artillery and surveillance" had been operating. The IDF stated Hezbollah uses medical facilities for terror activities. Residents in southern Lebanon, particularly Deir Zahrani, were displaced following Israeli threats. Lebanon's Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri accused Israel of using southern Lebanon as a "bloody ballot box" for its elections. Israeli forces informed residents in the north that a series of combat strikes would occur in the Lebanon front, with explosions heard in the Hula Valley, Ramim Ridge, and possibly the northern Golan.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, the US plans to withdraw all remaining troops and defense systems from the Kurdistan Region by September 30, under an agreement with the Iraqi government. US Patriot systems have been moved to Jordan, and British systems to Cyprus. The Kurdistan region's security institution reported three drone attacks on an Iranian refugee camp in Radash (Sulaymaniyah) between 04:45 and 05:05, with no injuries reported. Images showed destruction at Kurdish opposition group headquarters in Sulaymaniyah from these "suicide drone" attacks. Protests by oil institute graduates occurred in Baghdad in front of the Oil Ministry. A mass grave containing dozens of Popular Mobilization Forces and Iraqi Army martyrs, deceased 12 years ago, was discovered by chance during construction in Ramadi, Anbar province. In a move described as racist, Erbil municipality began removing Arabic signs from shops, requiring Kurdish language instead. A fire broke out in the Iraqi Minister of Education's home in Sadiya, west of Baghdad.

In Yemen, Houthi forces continue fighting government forces southwest of the country, pressing towards the port city of Mocha to gain control of the area near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Yemeni armed forces claimed to have shot down a Saudi CH-4 reconnaissance-attack drone over al-Jawf province and a Wing Loong II drone over Ta'izz province. Saudi forces reportedly targeted the border district of Shada with artillery shells. Yemeni armed forces announced a precise ballistic missile strike targeting a meeting of Saudi-backed forces.

In Syria, visual footage shows Israeli forces infiltrating Daraa province and establishing a military point.

GULF STATES
The UAE Presidential Advisor, Anwar Gargash, stated that dealing with Iran remains a pivotal issue for the UAE and other Gulf states, emphasizing that oil tankers and vessels cannot be subjected to continuous threats in the Strait of Hormuz. Oman has reportedly agreed with Iran on shipping lane maps in the Strait of Hormuz, with a signing expected in the coming days. Despite US military protection, oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 6.7 million barrels per day in the seven days through Thursday, nearly 60% below pre-war levels, according to the NYT. Kepler data showed average daily traffic at 10 vessels, with only 2 on Saturday and 6 on Sunday, mostly through Iranian-controlled waters. A CENTCOM spokesperson stated they assisted 1,600 commercial vessels and 800 million barrels of oil through the strait, claiming "commercial traffic flow continues... and momentum is clearly building." However, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed the US blockade had "choked" Iran's oil revenue and that exports had dwindled to zero. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei countered that the Strait is "completely closed" to US smuggling vessels, which Iran detects and sometimes strikes but doesn't sink to avoid environmental damage. A new burned area was observed around a crude oil storage tank at Saudi Aramco's Yanbu refinery on the Red Sea via Sentinel-2L satellite imagery. A fire of unknown origin occurred at Qatar's Ras Laffan station. Saudi-affiliated hackers reportedly seized control of the Nereida oil tanker flying the Comoros flag after it left the Port of Ras Isa.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions**: Iran's SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei claimed Iran tested an anti-destroyer missile over a US carrier 48 hours ago, forcing it to flee. He also announced Iran will declare a new "restricted zone" in the Persian Gulf in coming days, sanctioning uncoordinated vessels. This contradicts US CENTCOM claims of continued traffic and the US having redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled 3 Iranian tankers, and seized 2.
2.  **Israel-Lebanon Escalation**: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon, particularly Kfar Reman, reportedly killed at least 11 (including 2 children, 2 paramedics) and wounded 20, destroying a residential building and a Hezbollah command center in a former hospital. This was in response to a Hezbollah drone attack on Israeli troops at Ali Taher Ridge, which caused no Israeli casualties.
3.  **IDF Snap Drill**: The IDF conducted 'Breaking Dawn 2.0,' a surprise multi-front drill simulating terrorist infiltrations from Lebanon and Gaza, testing the General Staff's decision-making and overall readiness, which Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir stated was a "message to our enemies."
4.  **Iranian Fuel Price Hike**: The Iranian government officially increased fuel prices for "heavy consumers" (over 110 liters/month) by 100% to 100,000 Rials/liter, and the "third tier" gasoline price (for non-personal fuel cards) to 10,000 Tomans (100,000 Rials), effective 07 September. This led to widespread queuing at petrol stations.
5.  **Hamas Rocket/IED Incidents**: IDF/Yamam forces discovered a rocket (without launcher) and significant explosives during a raid in Aqqaba (West Bank) where 10 Hamas operatives were arrested. Separately, an IED attributed to Hamas hit an IDF engineering vehicle on the Gaza "Yellow Line," prompting Israeli airstrikes into Gaza, reportedly killing Hamas commander Yousef Akilah.
6.  **US Troop Withdrawal from Iraq**: The US will withdraw all remaining troops and defense systems from Iraq's Kurdistan Region by September 30, with Patriot systems moving to Jordan and British systems to Cyprus, under an agreement with the Iraqi government.
7.  **German Far-Right Electoral Success**: The far-right AfD party won a historic victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election with 44% of the vote (exit polls), becoming the largest party but falling short of an absolute majority. This is the first time since WWII a far-right party has led a German state.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The immediate escalation risk is high between Israel and Lebanon, as evidenced by extensive Israeli airstrikes in response to Hezbollah drone activity and IDF plans to destroy a Hezbollah underground complex. This could trigger a more substantial response from Hezbollah. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with Iran's explicit threats of a "restricted zone" and missile tests against US assets creating a volatile environment where miscalculation could lead to direct military conflict between Iran and the US. The US naval blockade and claimed strikes on Iranian tankers amplify this risk. Internally, Iran faces potential civil unrest due to the sudden and significant fuel price hike, which has historically been a trigger for protests. In the West Bank, settler violence and IDF raids continue to fuel tensions, increasing the likelihood of localized clashes and potential for broader unrest.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States**: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright indicated that a nuclear deal with Iran might not happen soon, possibly waiting for the next Iranian government, stating the US would continue to "destroy their capabilities." US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed the US blockade and sanctions had "choked" Iran's oil revenue and that exports had fallen to zero, with China having only about 30 million barrels left to buy. CENTCOM confirmed aiding 1,600 commercial vessels and 800 million barrels of oil through Hormuz, asserting "commercial traffic flow continues." US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv for direct negotiations with Ukrainian leadership. The US approved a new arms deal to Israel, including 10,000 smart bombs. The Pentagon refused compensation for soldiers killed in the "conflict" with Iran, arguing it's an operation, not a declared war. US President Trump continued strong rhetoric against Iran, sharing AI-generated images of strikes on Kharg Island ("Bye Bye Kharg") and claiming Iran is becoming a "failed state."

**Gulf States**: UAE Presidential Advisor Anwar Gargash emphasized the criticality of managing relations with Iran and the unacceptability of continuous threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz for Gulf states. Oman is reportedly finalizing shipping lane maps with Iran for Hormuz transit.

**Germany**: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure and French Minister for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad expressed "deep concern" over the far-right AfD's victory in Saxony-Anhalt, calling it a "serious moment for Europe." Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski also called it "a very worrying sign." CDU stated it would not form a coalition with either the far-right or the far-left. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov warned that accusations against Russia for the Leipzig airport drone attack amounted to the "start of a real war" with the West. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt plans to establish protective systems against Russian drone and cyberattacks.

**Russia**: Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that accusations by Germany regarding Russian involvement in the Leipzig airport drone incident marked "the start of a real war" with the West.

**North Korea**: Leader Kim Jong Un announced that the new 5,000-ton destroyer 'Kang Kon' would be part of the country's nuclear response system, capable of "annihilating retaliatory strikes," and asserted it was "time for us to exercise our sovereignty at sea and under water."

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are significant contradictions regarding the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei claimed the Strait is "completely closed" to US smuggling vessels, citing a recent missile test above a US carrier, and alleging that US attempts to smuggle 5-6 vessels often result in strikes. Conversely, US CENTCOM claims commercial traffic flows, they've assisted 1,600 vessels, and only 3 Iranian tankers were disabled/2 seized, refuting any Iranian strikes on US vessels as "completely false." Kepler's data shows significantly reduced traffic, indicating disruption, but not a complete closure. The US Treasury Secretary's claim of Iran's oil exports falling to "zero" is likely an overstatement or propaganda, as other sources still suggest some level of trade or reserves.

The number of casualties in Israeli strikes in Lebanon is inconsistent. NNA reported 11 dead and 5 wounded in Kfar Reman alone, while Lebanese health authorities later cited 4 dead and 20 wounded from strikes across southern Lebanon since morning. This discrepancy could be due to initial incomplete reports or a re-evaluation of the overall situation.

There is an unverified claim from a Russian journalist about Ukrainian drones sinking the Russian "shadow fleet" vessel Lady Maria in the Mediterranean, carrying Iranian weapons. This lacks official confirmation.

The ongoing political maneuvering in Israel, with numerous party list changes, mergers, and splits, suggests a fluid and potentially unstable pre-election environment. The "Yediotnews25" channel's list of Israeli election results from "Kan News" on September 7th, 2026, appears to be an *opinion poll* rather than actual election results, given the date (elections are 50 days away) and the context of party list submissions. This is an indicator of propaganda or misrepresentation of information.
